# Seed fixtures

The seed corpora the app fetches at runtime (`/data/vocabulary/**`, `/data/grammar/**`,
`/data/translations/**`) live in Supabase Storage. `public/data/**` is gitignored, so a CI checkout
has none of them, and the test fetch shim (`src/test/setup.ts`) used to answer every seed request by
calling the CDN. That made the suite depend on a live third party; when CI received a
`content-encoding`-less brotli body, sixteen tests across vocabulary, curriculum, orchestrator and
intelligence failed at once.

These files replace that: a small, committed, deterministic slice of each corpus, served from disk
by the shim so the suite reads the same bytes on every machine, with no network access at all.

## Provenance

Generated by `scripts/build-test-seed-fixtures.mjs` from a copy of the published corpus:

```bash
node scripts/build-test-seed-fixtures.mjs --source <dir with vocabulary/ grammar/ translations/>
```

The slices are not simply the first N entries. Each one keeps the properties the suites depend on:

| Slice                          | Must keep                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `vocabulary/a1.seed.json`      | A1 terms for the selection suite, ≥14 with `skillUse: speaking` (the orchestrator picks 10), ≥14 with `vocabulary`, and several distinct `domain` values (the domain filters) |
| `vocabulary/<level>.seed.json` | At least one term per CEFR level; B1 is split into `.seed.json` plus `.seed-1..3.json` exactly like the real corpus, so the shard merge stays covered                         |
| `grammar/a1.seed.json`         | Rules with `skillUse: speaking` and `canGenerateTaskTypes: speaking-production` (grammar selection for an A1 speaking task)                                                   |
| `grammar/<level>.seed.json`    | At least one rule per level                                                                                                                                                   |
| `translations/<lang>.json`     | `en`, `tr`, `ar`, each with at least one entry carrying a `meaning`                                                                                                           |

Every vocabulary and grammar entry is a real entry, so schema validation and every field the
selectors read behave exactly as they do against the full corpus.

## The corpus-integrity suites

Two suites assert on the corpus itself — its size, its duplicate-free term list, its domain
distribution — and cannot be satisfied by a slice. They run only when a real corpus copy is
configured, and skip with a reason otherwise:

```bash
ENGVOX_TEST_SEED_DIR=/path/to/corpus npm test
```

The shim looks in that directory first and falls back to these fixtures per file, so a partial copy
(for instance a local `public/data`, which has no grammar directory) is still usable. Nothing about
the default suite changes when the variable is set — it is only needed for those two suites.

`ENGVOX_TEST_SEED_FALLBACK=cdn` opts a run back into the network for seeds the configured sources
cannot serve. It exists to reach a corpus that is not on disk; the default path never touches the
network, and `src/test/seed-fixtures.test.ts` holds that guarantee in place.
